answer.reason: I cannot open the cited CSV directly, but a magnitude check against known BLS figures supports the draft (B) over the proposed correction (A). Arizona private covered employment in late 2024 was roughly 2.9-3.0 million jobs, and NAICS 54 (Professional, scientific, and technical services) has consistently run around 7.5-8% of Arizona private employment since about 2022, i.e., roughly 215,000-230,000 jobs, with December typically the highest month in Q4. The figure 226,731 fits that level well. By contrast, 177,356 would imply NAICS 54 is only about 6% of Arizona private employment - a level more consistent with Arizona's pre-2021 NAICS 54 employment (or possibly a sub-state or different-row value such as a county figure) than with December 2024 statewide private data. Independent anchors (national NAICS 54 share of ~8.3% of private covered employment, Arizona's professional-and-business-services composition, location quotient near 0.85-1.0, and plausible sector wage totals) all point to a December 2024 level in the low-to-mid 200,000s, not ~177,000. Therefore the draft answer B is the supported choice, and the proposed correction to A is not consistent with the known sector size.
